proof_summary: For consecutive primes \(p<q\), Wilson’s theorem and the factorization \((q-1)!=p!\bigl(\prod_{j=p+1}^{q-2}j\bigr)(q-1)\) give \(p!\prod_{j=p+1}^{q-2}j\equiv1\pmod q\), so either factor is \(1\) exactly when the other is. A gap of two makes the intervening product empty (and primality of \(p+2\) forces this gap), while a finite prime sieve identifies the 991st and 992nd primes as \(7841,7853\), and direct modular computation gives \(\prod_{j=7842}^{7851}j\equiv1\pmod{7853}\) for the exceptional index.
